lens: Sports game-film (Hudl): call replay timeline with scrubbing, tagged moments, coach annotations
name: Film Room Sideline
one_liner: Turn every practice call into game film: a scrubbable timeline with tagged moments, a live sideline HUD for coaching and scoring, and a launch library of 150+ forkable personas that a five-step AI wizard can extend, built on OpenAI models.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the Hudl lens closely: every call is stored as film with a timeline spine, auto-tagged moments (discovery, objection, pricing, close, filler) and coach and manager annotations pinned to timestamps. Changed two things after research. First, competitors split practice (Second Nature, Hyperbound), live assist (Cirrus Insight, Aircall) and post-call analysis (Gong) into separate products, so the timeline becomes one spine across all three phases. Second, Hudl's dense sports chrome would read as a sports app to insurance and mortgage reps, so the film room uses a calm neutral palette with teal and amber signal colours. Self-scores: A 8, B 8, C 8, F1 6, F2 6, F3 3 (3 = worth building).

ui_stack.name: shadcn/ui
ui_stack.role: Component base: Dialog, Sheet, Tabs, Slider, Command, Toast, Tooltip, Stepper patterns
ui_stack.why: Copy-in, owned source code with no runtime lock-in, which suits an MIT open-source project that contributors must read and change. Works with Next.js 15 and Tailwind. https://ui.shadcn.com/docs

ui_stack.name: Radix Primitives
ui_stack.role: Accessibility layer under shadcn (focus traps, ARIA for sheets, sliders, tabs, menus)
ui_stack.why: Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour for the live HUD and bottom sheets comes free and is battle-tested. https://www.radix-ui.com/

ui_stack.name: Tailwind CSS v4 (upgrade from v3)
ui_stack.role: Styling with the design tokens exposed as CSS variables in the theme
ui_stack.why: Replaces the hand-rolled .card and .btn-primary classes with tokens that drive light, dark and film surfaces from one source.

ui_stack.name: cmdk (via shadcn Command)
ui_stack.role: Cmd-K palette for persona, scenario and action search across 150+ entries
ui_stack.why: Contributors and reps find a persona by objection or industry in one keystroke.

ui_stack.name: Motion (motion.dev, formerly Framer Motion)
ui_stack.role: Layout transitions, cue-card entrance, meter tweens, playhead movement
ui_stack.why: Declarative motion that is easy for contributors to change and honours prefers-reduced-motion.

ui_stack.name: wavesurfer.js (regions plugin)
ui_stack.role: Waveform and scrubbable timeline for call audio, with coloured regions for tagged moments
ui_stack.why: Gives the film strip real audio in voice mode and text-timed markers in text mode, the core of the Hudl lens.

ui_stack.name: TanStack Table and Recharts
ui_stack.role: Film library table, team heatmap and criterion trend charts
ui_stack.why: Sortable and filterable tables plus simple, accessible charts without a heavy dashboard framework. Use the dataviz skill palette rules for chart colours.

ui_stack.name: Sora, Inter, JetBrains Mono
ui_stack.role: Display, UI and timestamp or score typography
ui_stack.why: Sora and Inter are already in the app, so the change stays recognisable. Mono gives timestamps and token costs tabular alignment.

ui_stack.name: zod (existing)
ui_stack.role: One persona and rubric schema shared by the wizard, the JSON pack importer and CI validation
ui_stack.why: Keeps community-contributed personas valid without a second schema to maintain.

palette.use: Light page background for landing, library, progress and team views (dark mode uses --film).
Dark film surface for the live call stage, timeline strip and debrief film room.
Primary text on light surfaces (about 17:1 on --canvas).
Primary actions such as Start call and Create with AI (white text about 5.5:1).
Live playhead, good live scores and focus rings on dark surfaces (about 12:1 on --film).
Whisper cues and missed-moment tags; ink text sits on it at about 11:1.
Objection alerts and risk tags on dark; light mode swaps to #BE123C.

design_language.typography: Sora 600-700 for screen titles and grade numerals; Inter 400-600 for UI and transcripts (16px transcript, 14px UI); JetBrains Mono 500 with tabular-nums for timestamps, scores and token costs. Titles 28-40px.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 14px cards, 10px controls, pill chips. 1px hairlines instead of soft shadows. Film surfaces get a faint top-light gradient and an inner border. The blurry orb becomes a live voice waveform, so the persona visibly speaks.
design_language.motion: Panels 180-240ms ease-out; playhead follows audio time via requestAnimationFrame; score bars tween over 400ms; the cue card enters at most once every 20 seconds; all motion is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: Lucide at 1.75 stroke (already used). Six custom moment-tag glyphs (discovery, objection, pricing, close, filler, rapport) drawn on the same 24px grid. No emoji.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default for landing, library, progress and team. Film-dark is the default for live call and debrief timeline. Both are CSS-variable themes that follow the system setting with a manual toggle. All text pairs meet WCAG AA.

navigation_and_ia: Top bar with five items: Practice (home), Library, Calls, Progress, and Team (shown only when an org exists). A Cmd-K palette and one New call button sit on the right. Mobile uses a bottom tab bar with the same five items. Library holds the filterable catalogue and the Create with AI button. Calls lists every film, searchable by persona, objection and tag. Login, access code and MFA move behind one account menu. Scenario editing becomes the wizard's Review step and a per-persona Edit drawer.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Self-score D: 6. Coaching runs as a separate coach call that reads each finished rep turn plus a short interim transcript, and returns at most one cue: a next-best question, an objection alert or a checkpoint nudge. Cues are throttled (one at a time, 20-second minimum gap) and shown only to the rep. The persona never receives them, so it stays in character. Scoring is incremental: each turn moves the six rubric meters, and every number carries the transcript line that the debrief reuses, so live and final scores cannot disagree. In voice mode, cues can be spoken through a second audio channel, which needs headphones. The open risk is latency and cue accuracy. The first milestone is a measured harness over recorded calls, not UI polish.
persona_library_and_wizard: Self-score E: 6. Ship a launch pack of 150+ persona-scenario pairs (target) as one versioned JSON pack in the repo, organised by job, industry, difficulty and objection type. Each entry has a rubric and two scripted replies for offline tests. One zod schema validates every entry in the wizard, the importer and CI. The wizard turns a URL, job description, ICP, CRM note or pasted call into a draft persona, shows the extracted facts for review, and exports a PR-ready file. Sources stay in the browser unless the user sets a key; a URL is fetched only when the user asks. Built-ins remain read-only and forkable, as they are today.
signature_moments: The timeline is the spine: scrub any call, and every tag, score and coach note is pinned to a timestamp on the same strip.
A cue card that appears only when it matters, one at a time, and the persona never hears it.
Rubric meters that move during the call, so the rep watches each criterion change line by line.
Replay this moment: a debrief tag starts a retake from that timestamp with the same persona.
Persona cards carry their objections as chips, so the library reads like a playbook.
Every AI output shows the model that produced it and what it cost in tokens and dollars.
openai_fund_angle: Make OpenAI visible where it does real work. The live HUD and debrief show a model strip (Realtime voice, coach model, grader model) and a cost line per call. The README explains each OpenAI piece and how API credits would be used. Codex is used concretely: the repo's CI runs Codex CLI to review persona-pack PRs for schema, bias and rubric weights, and maintainer automation drafts release notes. A Contribute page shows those checks as badges on merged personas. Contributors are invited through the wizard's Export as PR file, good-first-issue labels and a credit line on each community persona card. This matches the Codex open source fund (grants up to $25K in API credits for projects using Codex CLI and OpenAI models) and the Codex for Open Source uses: PR review, maintainer automation and release workflows.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0 (week 1): upgrade Tailwind 3 to 4, add shadcn/ui and Radix, move tokens to CSS variables, keep routes and take visual baseline screenshots. Phase 1: shared shell, persona JSON pack and zod schema, Pre-call and live HUD behind a feature flag. Phase 2: debrief film room with the timeline, then the wizard. Phase 3: progress, team view, mobile polish, README and GIF refresh, and the CI Codex check. Existing localStorage scenarios and the grading API stay unchanged, with an importer that maps old scenarios into the new schema.

risks: Live coaching latency and cue accuracy are unproven. Without a measured harness over recorded calls, D stays at baseline and the HUD is decoration.
Hudl-style density can read as sports-coded. Test the palette with real insurance and mortgage reps before locking it.
A 150-persona pack is a content job. Ship about 40 hand-checked personas first and generate the rest through the wizard with human review.
Pasted real calls contain customer PII. Strip it before any model call and before export, or the wizard becomes a compliance problem.
Voice-mode cues need headphones; without them the cue can bleed into the mic and the persona may hear coaching.
Defaulting to OpenAI ties the fund story to vendor pricing. Keep OpenAI-compatible endpoints and a local-only mode so the core works without credits.
The Tailwind 4 migration touches every screen. Freeze visual regression baselines before starting.
Manager visibility and recording need consent labels and retention rules before any team pilot (F2).
